races.name: Coca-Cola HBC Ireland And Northern Ireland 3-Y-O Hurdle

runners_data.name: Nicky Larson
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, Paul Nolan's charge has form on Good ground and steps up in trip having finished first and third in recent starts; his ability to control the gallop makes him pivotal to every scenario, though a STYLE_FIT flag suggests he may not be entirely at home dictating here.
runners_data.comment: Nicky Larson arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, giving him a solid profile at the head of the weights on 158 lb; 18 days between runs is plenty fresh enough to go again.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon runner with a fade-in-finish flag who ran just eight days ago, and the short turnaround alongside modest hurdles form (0U) raises significant stamina and soundness queries over this 2m1½f trip on quick ground.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Camp Verde has been yet to win in his last two starts — including an unseating — but returns quickly after just eight days and, lightly raced, there is plenty more to learn about him.

runners_data.name: Fay Og
runners_data.note: W R Crawford's hold-up specialist is honestly a rear-group horse, but the preponderance of hold-up types in this field means it is shown in midfield — 102 days off the track, three poor recent runs including a last-of-eight on Good, and a fade concern all weigh heavily against.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Fay Og has had time to develop over 102 days away and carries 152 lb on his first start — connections will be hoping he can make an immediate impact.

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner brings the field's most consistent placing pattern on Good ground and has been placed twice in ten similar-going runs; operates as a genuine hold-up horse whose ability to close through a compressed field gives it realistic claims if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Nod Of Approval catches the eye on his profile here, carrying 152 lb on a competitive mark and returning on a lively 18-day turnaround with our rating of 83 placing him third in the field; the risk is that he is yet to score in recent starts, that sole effort a seventh.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's lightly raced debutant with an UNKNOWN going profile and a 7lb claimer in Thomas O'Connor; impossible to map with any confidence and must be treated as a wildcard until more evidence is available.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Point Star is a complete unknown but lightly raced profiles like his often leave room for significant improvement; carrying 152 lb on his first start, he is yet to score but there is plenty to learn about him here.

runners_data.name: Moon Aura
runners_data.note: Kevin Sexton's mount for C A McBratney has a naturally prominent style and consistent Good-ground profile, though five runs without a win and a pattern of mid-division finishes (6,6,4,6,8) suggest it is competitive without being a winner.
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore unexposed, Moon Aura steps into the unknown on debut after 59 days off the track, carrying 145 lb, with plenty of potential still to be uncovered.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's yard is in strong form (6/34 in 14 days) and this horse has solid recent form figures of 3 and 4 on Good ground, making it arguably the most interesting hold-up runner; it is a true rear-group horse pushed into a midfield position by the field's makeup, meaning it needs things to fall right tactically.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and fourth two starts back, No Bother Aoife arrives fit on an 18-day turnaround with distance experience to call on and a rating of 90 that marks her out as a leading threat; the risk is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Adrian Sexton's runner carries a fade-in-finish flag alongside headgear (hood) and a patchy record that includes placing only once from five similar-going runs; on the evidence available it looks up against it in this company.
runners_data.comment: Sands Castle has been off for just 18 days and returns at a workable weight of 145 lb, with our rating of 79 marking her as a genuine player in this field; the main concern is that she heads here winless from her last start and must find improvement.

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Crawford's second runner, a true hold-up horse with a fade-in-finish concern, headgear (hood/tongue-tie), and 55 days off the track; three placed efforts at shorter trips suggest stamina for this distance is not guaranteed, and the style flag compounds the task.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Swift Charm steps into the spotlight here carrying 145 lb after a 55-day absence, yet to score but with plenty still to find out about her.

races.paceDynamic: Nicky Larson is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 3-y-o hurdle and, with no rival likely to seriously press for the lead, he can control tempo from the front on his own terms over 2m1½f on Good to Firm ground at Down Royal. Camp Verde and Moon Aura are the only other runners with a naturally prominent profile, but neither is a confirmed pace-setter, meaning Nicky Larson dictates without a genuine challenger breathing down his neck. This creates a sustainable, measured gallop that could turn the race into a procession for those travelling just behind the pace — a premium position in this shape — with hold-up horses required to make up ground against horses who have never been off the bridle. The race shape strongly favours a prominent or close-tracking profile that can latch onto Nicky Larson's tail early, travel within his slipstream, and produce a clean jump at the last; true hold-up horses face an uphill task on a track where the finish is not long enough to reel back a well-paced leader. Note that the field contains more hold-up types than can genuinely race at the rear: No Bother Aoife and Fay Og are redistributed to midfield on the map, but both are true hold-up horses who may struggle to find their natural position and whose chances are discounted accordingly in a race shape that rewards proximity to the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nicky Larson Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Nicky Larson bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair, even tempo that suits his jumping rhythm.
scenarios.body: Nicky Larson travels on the bridle at the head of affairs, takes each hurdle efficiently, and a prominent rival who tracks him throughout seizes the advantage at the last when Nicky Larson's 3-y-o stamina tests. Camp Verde and Moon Aura are next best positioned to deliver a late prominent challenge, though both carry their own form concerns at this level.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-to-midfield horse tracks Nicky Larson comfortably and produces a decisive jump at the final flight.
scenarios.body: A horse travelling just off the leader's heels is perfectly placed when Nicky Larson ties up or makes a jumping error in the closing stages, allowing a clean-jumping challenger to quicken past on the run-in. No Bother Aoife, if it gets closer to the pace than its natural style suggests, and Nod Of Approval from the hold-up group are the most likely beneficiaries if fatigue claims the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Nicky Larson sets an overly fast tempo and the front pack fades dramatically in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A hot early pace would open up ground for genuine hold-up runners to pick up the pieces down the straight, although both No Bother Aoife and Fay Og are redistributed hold-up types racing out of their natural position, making this scenario structurally weaker than the probability alone suggests. Nod Of Approval's consistent placing record in similar good-ground conditions gives it the best profile among the rear-group contenders if the race does fall apart for the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Errors, Wide Open
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the front two or three and the race fractures into multiple small groups.
scenarios.body: Camp Verde's hurdles form is fragile and an early mistake could string the field out, handing an advantage to any horse that jumps cleanly through the chaos. Swift Charm and Sands Castle carry fading-in-finish flags that limit their appeal even in an open scenario, but a clean-jumping opportunist emerging from the pack cannot be entirely ruled out.

watchPoints.text: Nicky Larson's jumping must be monitored from the front — if he makes an error at an early flight he loses his tactical advantage immediately and Camp Verde or Moon Aura could exploit the gap.
Camp Verde's fade-in-finish flag combined with running just eight days ago makes it a serious risk to backers: watch for it stopping quickly after the second-last if the pace has been at all honest.

No Bother Aoife is being mapped to midfield but is genuinely a hold-up horse — if Gavin Cromwell's runner cannot get cover and is forced wider than ideal in the early stages, its chance is materially reduced.
Point Star is an unknown quantity making what appears to be a hurdles debut; watch the market and paddock for any confidence signal from the Mark Fahey camp before treating it as a live contender.

Fay Og's 102-day absence and three consecutive poor runs on comparable ground make it difficult to trust at face value — watch whether J J Slevin asks for more in the early stages, which would suggest the yard believes it is ready to run to its best.

races.name: Dale Farm Dromona Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cosmic Front
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner returning after a 203-day break with a strong flat form profile; races prominently and should slot in just behind Loughdoo, and the Good to Firm surface suits his form at Sligo and Leopardstown on similar ground.

runners_data.name: Churchfield Annie
runners_data.note: Has form on good ground with four of five runs on good to firm or good, races prominently, and her consistency in placing (0W 3P) suggests she travels well but needs to improve her finishing effort; tongue tie noted and 47 days since last run is manageable.

runners_data.name: Howaya Codge
runners_data.note: Has form on good ground and returns on a short 20-day turnaround; her true running style is hold-up but the volume of hold-up types in this field means she will be squeezed out of her natural position — she ran on good ground last time and finished tenth, which is a slim base for confidence.

runners_data.name: Jo's Secret
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with good-ground form from multiple runs, placing twice in similar conditions; sits slightly closer to the pace than a pure closer, and at 55 days since last run her freshness could be an asset if the race develops late.

runners_data.name: Loughdoo
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner; fades in finish flag is a concern over the trip, but with no rivals willing to press hard from the front she can control the gallop and may conserve enough to hold on; 22 days since last run and a 7lb claimer aboard adds an element of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Messonghi
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only one hurdle start, a fall on good ground; the unknown quantity in the field and the limited evidence means any assessment carries significant caveats — could progress sharply or could be exposed as too raw.

runners_data.name: Saoirses Choice
runners_data.note: Has finished ninth twice in similar good-ground maiden hurdle company and her "fades in finish" flag underlines a recurring pattern; hold-up style in a race where closers face structural disadvantages makes it hard to be enthusiastic here.

runners_data.name: Clanokre Lass
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained four-year-old with three runs, all on good ground, placing fourth in her second start; her natural running style is hold-up but with so many hold-up types in the field she has been placed in midfield on the map — her STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers her realistic chance of striking from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Rare Times
runners_data.note: Lower official rating at 95 but has placed twice on good ground and races prominently; J J Slevin aboard is a significant jockey booking and she is 14 days fresh — her prominent style suits this race shape well and her consistent placing record is the main angle.

runners_data.name: Tanga Mugi
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with headgear applied; sole hurdle run produced a seventh on good ground and her flat form showed a win, but jumping the trip with limited data is the key unknown — the headgear change could sharpen her early, but her natural style works against her here.

runners_data.name: That's It Girl
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell runner making her debut over hurdles with going listed as unknown and no days-since-last-run data available; the Cromwell yard has been 6/34 in the last 14 days which shows form, but nothing in the data supports a confident style or going assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Loughdoo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, despite carrying a "fades in finish" flag, should control the early tempo unchallenged from the front, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop on Good to Firm ground over 2m1½f. Cosmic Front and Churchfield Annie will press forward from a prominent position, with Rare Times also likely to race prominently, creating a clear pace hierarchy without any genuine rival willing to burn Loughdoo off early. The race therefore shapes as a single-file lead contest with a controlled tempo that will not collapse early, meaning the race is likely to be decided on jumping fluency and the ability to sustain effort into the final two hurdles rather than on a brutal finishing kick from deep. This shape firmly favours the prominent and front-running profiles — horses sitting on or near the pace, travelling within themselves, who can simply outstay a moderate hold-up challenge; Cosmic Front and Churchfield Annie are best placed positionally, while the true hold-up horses Howaya Codge and Clanokre Lass have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more deep-seated hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Loughdoo is the only runner likely to fully secure its natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Loughdoo sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided by those travelling prominently into the straight.
scenarios.body: Loughdoo dictates a sensible tempo and those sitting closest — Cosmic Front and Churchfield Annie — travel comfortably and have enough in reserve to overhaul the leader approaching the last; the Good to Firm surface rewards horses who travel fluently rather than grind late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally faster than anticipated and the leaders tire late, allowing a midfield tracker to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Jo's Secret or Rare Times, sitting slightly off the early pace in a comfortable rhythm, benefit from a modest fade in the front group and close strongly on the run-in; the Good to Firm ground aids their ability to maintain stride length to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Loughdoo and the early pace group sustain their effort and the pace proves too strong for those trying to close.
scenarios.body: Loughdoo's uncontested lead allows it to control every yard and, if the fading tendency is less pronounced today, it could simply outlast a moderate staying challenge; the lack of any real pace duel means it never burns through its energy reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses unexpectedly and a hold-up horse manages to secure a position close enough to strike late.
scenarios.body: With Howaya Codge and Clanokre Lass operating out of their natural role and mapped to midfield, this scenario depends on true hold-up runners getting closer than expected, which is a low-probability outcome given the race shape; a very rough race with positional reshuffling would be the prerequisite.

watchPoints.text: Loughdoo sets every yard alone — watch whether Harry Sexton (7lb claim) dictates a genuinely economical pace or allows the tempo to drift, as the entire race shape hinges on this one runner's control.

Cosmic Front returns after 203 days off for Willie Mullins; watch his jumping in the early stages, as a prominent runner rusty over hurdles after a long absence could unsettle the race shape around the first few flights.

Clanokre Lass and Howaya Codge are both true hold-up horses likely to be outpositioning themselves in midfield — watch whether they get caught wide or are hampered in traffic, as their displaced running style creates a hidden risk for others around them.

Rare Times is the standout prominent runner with a jockey upgrade to J J Slevin; watch whether she tracks Cosmic Front and Churchfield Annie and effectively creates more pressure on Loughdoo than the pace map anticipates.
That's It Girl is a complete unknown on debut for Cromwell — watch her price drifts and early jumping to gauge whether she is here to learn or is expected to be competitive on the day.

races.name: Golden Cow Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lips Freedom
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a winning profile on Good ground and a fade-in-finish flag that makes her reliant on a truly run race — 16-runner field with compressed midfield traffic is a concern; 27 days fresh.|
runners_data.comment: Lips Freedom has two wins in his last five starts and has experience over today's trip, with 27 days since his last run suggesting he returns fresh; the main risk is that he was unplaced last time out, so he must bounce back to his best.

runners_data.name: Bannow Blaze
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose recent form string shows unseat and falls — jumping reliability is the key issue here rather than pace position; handles similar going but question marks over consistency.|
runners_data.comment: Bannow Blaze finished second five starts back but has endured a torrid run since, pulling up, falling and unseating in his last three outings; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating just edges him to the top, though market confidence may hinge on whether that turbulent recent spell is behind him.

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish but has the ability to place — A J Martin's yard in moderate recent form (T14: 0/6), ran well over 21f on Good; this trip and surface suit but the fade flag limits winning prospects in a slowly-run race.|
runners_data.comment: Bruant won three starts back and returned to form with a second last time out, showing he retains plenty of ability off a mark of 110; he has run over today's trip before, but the 166 lb burden is the one factor that could blunt his challenge.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner whose STYLE_FIT score (0.93) warns he is racing out of natural role; has won at 17f on Good and should land a prominent position by default in this field, but sustained front-running is not his proven forte.|
runners_data.comment: Hopeful Hero showed plenty two starts back with a win, but was unplaced on his most recent outing and faces a stiff task under 165 lb; he has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days off, leaving connections hopeful of a bounce-back.

runners_data.name: Only For Our Man
runners_data.note: Strong staying hold-up profile with five placings in five recent runs over 19-24f — this trip at 2m1½f may be on the sharp side, but Paul Nolan's yard has a runner at 1/4 over 14 days and James Smith takes the 5lb claim.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent, with a win among his last five, Only For Our Man has finished second twice and third last time out in lively recent form, though 43 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and carries a hefty 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Three wins from 15 similar-going runs and won over this trip 14 days ago — the quick return is notable, but P E Collins has a recent winner (T14: 1/2) and the horse clearly thrives fresh on Good ground.|
runners_data.comment: Small Bucks won last time out and has run over today's trip, but her patchy recent record — two wins alongside two unplaced efforts in her last six starts — and a ranking of 11th in this field suggest she faces a stiff ask under 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the mount for Gordon Elliott on a horse that has placed prominently in multiple recent starts on Good ground — genuine prominent type well-placed to sit second or third and deliver his effort from the second-last.|
runners_data.comment: Dairy Force shaped well enough last time when third, and was second three starts back and fourth starts back, yet winless in recent starts and burdened by 160 lb alongside a trainer operating at just 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Kazakh d'Arthel
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose natural racing position is at the rear, though the sheer number of closers in this field means he is unlikely to race there in practice; Gavin Cromwell in excellent 14-day form (6/34), but STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) signals a potential positional compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Kazakh d'Arthel won in his last five starts but has since posted a fourth, a fall, and two disappointing efforts, leaving his current form in question; he has run over today's trip and returns after 43 days off carrying 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton (7) takes over on a five-year-old whose natural instinct is to race from the back — pressed forward by field size, the horse will be racing in unnatural territory; has won on Good ground and handles this trip, but the redistribution muddles his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Mo Ghille Mar won four starts back but has since posted a pair of sevenths and a fourth, leaving her form looking patchy; she has run over today's trip and comes here 26 days fresh, though 160 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Certamen
runners_data.note: Prominent-style handler with headgear (tongue-pin) and zero wins or places from eight similar-going runs — no evidence of the form required to exploit a prominent position; Edward Buckley yard winless in 14 days (0/4).|
runners_data.comment: Certamen arrives on the back of a pull-up last time and is winless in his last four starts, which makes him hard to trust, though 25 days in between runs suggests he returns reasonably fresh and he is not without ability on a rating of 105.

runners_data.name: Golden Wings
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's second string, a genuine hold-up specialist mapped into midfield by field congestion; zero wins or places from five similar-going runs and a recent string of poor efforts suggest limited immediate hope regardless of scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up and two deep finishes among recent efforts, Golden Wings faces a stiff ask off 158 lb for a trainer firing at just 3% lately; experience over today's trip is the one crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Viceregent
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning after a 310-day layoff — the lengthy absence is the dominant concern; a true hold-up horse whose distance and surface form is all at shorter trips than today's 2m1½f on Good to Firm.|
runners_data.comment: Rated 114 and ranked second of 16, Viceregent shaped with plenty of promise when fourth and fifth in recent starts, and that form makes him a serious threat on a return from 310 days off — though his pulled-up latest effort and winless run in his last five starts are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has a dire recent record (three consecutive single-figure finishes); a natural hold-up type whose redistribution into midfield compresses an already limited chance, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.91) is well-warranted.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom two on our figures, Home By The Sea faces a stiff ask at 154 lb, though a return to action after just 18 days at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's yard in strong recent form (3/12 over 14 days) and the horse has won over this trip and distance on Good ground — a genuine hold-up type forced into midfield by field size, but the trainer angle and proven course-distance ability make this one worth monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the principals on our figures, Kilt has managed just one win in his last five starts, with three fourth-or-worse efforts since, and carrying 154 lb does him no favours; he has run over today's trip before, and 25 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Whispering Willow
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell fields two here; this five-year-old won on Good ground over 16f and placed over 19-20f — trip suits, but a true rear-runner operating in a congested midfield, and recent form shows a decline (13360).|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Whispering Willow is hard to fancy despite a win and two thirds in recent starts; she has run over today's trip and returns after 35 days, but her last two outings — unplaced and sixth — make a turnaround difficult to argue for.

runners_data.name: Your Call
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a blinker flag and a poor recent record — eighth from eight on Good ground with zero wins or places, and Caragh Monaghan's claim does little to mask a horse that has consistently struggled in similar conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Your Call faces a stiff ask off 151 lb; he has run over today's trip and returns after 45 days, but an eighth last time out offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Hopeful Hero is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, despite a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting this is not his most natural role, Michael Kenneally will likely push him to the front from the gates, setting what should be a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Down Royal. With only Dairy Force and Certamen as genuine prominent types to keep him honest, the pace is unlikely to be fierce, meaning the early tempo will be metronomic rather than punishing — a classic single-pace-setter scenario where the leader dictates terms and few can chase him hard. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear; Kazakh d'Arthel, Mo Ghille Mar, Golden Wings, Viceregent, Home By The Sea, Kilt, Whispering Willow and Your Call are all true sit-and-wait horses compressed into a congested midfield, with Dairy Force and Certamen the most likely to actually secure the prominent berths directly behind Hopeful Hero. This race shape — a lone leader setting honest but uncontested fractions — strongly favours prominent-tracking types who can travel smoothly in behind the pace and produce their effort from two out, rather than true hold-up horses who will need a searching gallop to create the gaps they require late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hopeful Hero Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Hopeful Hero is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and set a fair but unexacting tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Kenneally dictates every fraction from the front, the pack never applies meaningful pressure, and the race turns into a test of jumping accuracy and staying power from two out. Prominent trackers who travel economically and jump well are ideally positioned to run on as the leader ties up or is picked off close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce Two Out
scenarios.trigger: If Dairy Force or another prominent type travels powerfully in second or third and strikes for home before the last.
scenarios.body: A smooth-travelling prominent racer exploits the well-organised pace by lobbing into contention and producing a clean jump at the second-last to open a decisive gap. Hold-up horses further back are too far off the pace on a sound surface to close the distance in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from three out, stretching the field and creating room for genuine hold-up types to thread through.
scenarios.body: A genuinely fast-run finish on Good to Firm ground would expose the front-runners and compress the finishers into a tight bundle, allowing a horse like Small Bucks or Kilt — who have proven ability on this surface — to weave through. This scenario is partially discounted because several mapped midfielders are redistributed hold-up horses unlikely to get a true staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Hopeful Hero jumps flawlessly and the pack misjudges the pace, leaving him unchallenged to the line.
scenarios.body: In a race with chaotic hold-up congestion, the field may collectively underestimate the leader's continued gallop and fail to organise a coherent pursuit. This is the least likely shape because Hopeful Hero is flagged as racing out of role and the STYLE_FIT discount significantly tempers confidence in him sustaining the effort.

watchPoints.text: Dairy Force (Jack Kennedy/Gordon Elliott) is the most dangerous horse in the race if he secures a prominent position behind Hopeful Hero — Kennedy's ability to travel handily and produce at the second-last could prove decisive if the pace is controlled.
Small Bucks runs back just 14 days after a win over this exact trip on Good ground — watch whether the quick return dulls his finishing effort or whether Collins has him primed for a bold follow-up.

Midfield congestion is extreme with eight or more genuine hold-up types compressed behind the leaders — watch for significant interference and traffic issues at the hurdles from the third-last onwards as horses attempt to find gaps simultaneously.

Hopeful Hero's STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) means the race shape hinges on a horse racing out of role — if Kenneally cannot sustain the front-running task past three out, the race could collapse into a sprint finish that suits different profiles entirely.

Kilt (P J Rothwell, 3/12 in 14 days) is a trainer-in-form angle to note if he secures a clean passage through the congested midfield — proven on this trip and going, and the yard's current strike rate gives the runner a quiet each-way claim.

races.name: Pepsico (Walkers Snacks) Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hidden Empire
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one hurdles start (finished 8th on soft), making this a big step into the unknown; the style data flags a tendency to fade in the finish which is a concern over 2m4f on quick ground, and this is a horse that needs to prove it stays.

runners_data.name: Santa Domingo
runners_data.note: 335 days off the track — the longest absence in the field — yet trainer John McConnell sends him out fit enough to front-run; his sole hurdles run was a promising second on soft over 10f but stepping to 2m4f first-time back is a significant query, and the STYLE_FIT flag notes he may not fully dominate as anticipated.

runners_data.name: Seamy Appletart
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has shown zero threat in two hurdles starts (5th, 11th) on good ground, going 0-from-2 in similar conditions; 45 days off the track and a maiden trainer strike rate of 0/0 in the 14-day window give little confidence this is a horse primed for a bold showing.

runners_data.name: Teddy Jones
runners_data.note: Like Hidden Empire, is lightly raced with one run to his name — a distant 9th on soft — and carries the same flags around fading in the finish; Donagh Meyler takes the ride but there is very little form to anchor expectations at a distance demanding stamina.

runners_data.name: Wackestone
runners_data.note: Has raced six times over hurdles with a best of 2nd on soft and consistently prominent racing style suits this pace scenario well; Gordon Elliott's yard are 1/30 in the 14-day window which is modest, and the horse wears a hood — noteworthy on fast ground where it could sharpen focus.

runners_data.name: Wee Fallon
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish according to the style data and has finished 13th, 7th and 8th in her three jumps starts, going 0-from-3 on similar ground; 24 days between runs and a young claimer aboard suggest this is a horse still finding her feet at this level.

runners_data.name: Lisnadill
runners_data.note: Best flat form shows two placed efforts at shorter trips on good ground, but over hurdles she has consistently finished well back (14th twice, 13th, 6th); a genuine hold-up horse whose map position understates how far she'll be taken back in running — the style mismatch dampens her prospects in this strongly pace-controlled shape.

runners_data.name: Oops A Daisy
runners_data.note: Three hurdles starts all on good ground, all finishing 7th or worse, and the fade-in-finish flag is a consistent theme; naturally a rear-of-field type who will find it difficult to get into her preferred spot with so many hold-up horses in the field, and the STYLE_FIT discount is merited given the race shape is unlikely to set up for a late charge.

races.paceDynamic: Santa Domingo is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, should be able to dictate at a sustainable, controlled tempo on good-to-firm ground over 2m4f. Wackestone is the only other prominent-profile runner and will likely sit in behind, meaning the pace is set by one horse rather than a genuine duel — a scenario that historically favours those travelling well just off the bridle rather than deep closers. Both Lisnadill and Oops A Daisy are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate at the back; neither is likely to secure their natural position as freely as they would prefer. The controlled, single-setter tempo on fast ground over a staying hurdle trip decisively favours prominent or tracking runners who can travel within themselves and quicken on the turn for home — a flat-out slog that suits grinders is unlikely given the going and the absence of pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Santa Domingo Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Santa Domingo bowls along unchallenged and the pace remains honest but not punishing, leaving prominent trackers ideally placed.
scenarios.body: Santa Domingo sets a metronomic gallop and any horse travelling comfortably just off the pace, within a length or two, gets the perfect tow into the straight; on good-to-firm the premium is on horses who handle quick ground and stay the trip rather than those who need a slog.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just steady enough that a horse tracking in second or third cruises past a tiring Santa Domingo from two out.
scenarios.body: A horse like Wackestone, accustomed to racing prominently, gets a dream position in second and has enough left to collar the leader when the gap opens up turning in; good-to-firm suits this profile and the 2m4f trip is within range.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Santa Domingo goes too quick early on fast ground and blows up before the final flight, leaving the field strung out.
scenarios.body: A horse able to pick up from midfield when the pace implodes could swoop late, though this is blunted by the fact that Lisnadill and Oops A Daisy — the most natural closers — are true hold-up types already pushed forward and unlikely to be in a genuine late-running position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If early trouble, jumping errors or fallers disrupt the field and the race becomes a messy slog for an unexposed type.
scenarios.body: An unexposed or lightly-raced runner such as Hidden Empire or Teddy Jones — both with limited hurdles form — could benefit if the normal hierarchy is scrambled and raw ability over form becomes the deciding factor.

watchPoints.text: Watch Santa Domingo's early jumping — a 335-day absence means any hesitation at the early flights could cost him the lead and unravel the entire pace map.

Wackestone wears a hood for the first time or as a recurring piece of headgear; if it has a sharpening effect he could be quicker away than expected and pressurise Santa Domingo, turning a controlled pace into a genuine duel.

Lisnadill and Oops A Daisy are genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield on the map — if they drift further back than shown and the pace is not strong enough, they may find themselves with too much ground to make up in the straight.

The going is officially Good to Firm throughout the card at Down Royal, confirmed by multiple races — any horse whose form reads predominantly on soft ground (Hidden Empire, Santa Domingo, Teddy Jones) faces an untested question on this surface.

Three riders in this field are claiming jockeys — James Smith (5), Michael Kenneally (5) and Joshua Halford (7) — adding an element of positional uncertainty, particularly if inexperience leads to overcrowding behind the leader in the early stages.

races.name: Denny Hurdle

runners_data.name: Reverend Hubert
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with strong staying form on Good ground — four wins in similar conditions — and trainer C Byrnes has 0/6 over the past 14 days, but this horse's raw course record makes it a live each-way player if the pace collapses late; hood noted.
runners_data.comment: Reverend Hubert returns 30 days on from a winning effort two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims here; the 164 lb burden is a factor to weigh, though his recent record of two wins in his last five starts underlines his ability.

runners_data.name: Loch Cuan
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott five-year-old who has won two of his last three on Good ground over 22f and ran well in defeat at similar trips — prominent style suits this pace scenario ideally and a 5lb claim from James Smith eases the weight burden.
runners_data.comment: Loch Cuan arrives on the back of consecutive wins and has solid recent form, but he is ranked eighth of nine on our figures, carries a hefty 160 lb, and his trainer has managed just one winner from 37 runners in the past fortnight — considerable negatives to weigh against that winning momentum.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here and OR-rated 147, the class horse in the field; has won on similar going and returns 14 days after a run, with trainer Declan Queally 1/6 in the past fortnight — his ability to control tempo from the front is his greatest asset but also his primary vulnerability if the duel with The Friday Man proves costly.
runners_data.comment: Rocky's Diamond arrives here in solid heart, winning two starts back and running third last time out, while experience over today's trip and a return after just 14 days underlines his readiness — the pull-up three starts back remains the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has scrambled in the frame at 18-22f on Good ground and is fit off a 14-day return; Keith Donoghue is a reliable pilot in staying hurdles and the horse's ability to produce a late rattle suits if the pace has done its damage, though his sim-going record (1W2P from 15) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Thecompanysergeant arrives on the back of a fourth last time out, but he showed his true colours with a win three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and a sharp 14-day turnaround keep him firmly in the mix; the 159 lb burden is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Clay Pigeons
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained prominent type with a strong record on Good to Soft but only one run on Good proper; the trip at 3m is a step up and the headgear (tongue tie) is noted, but Brian Hayes keeps this competitive and its recent form (1/12-1) is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Rattled off wins in three of his last four starts, with a second two starts back the only blemish, and 24 days between runs keeps him fresh; at 155 lb and rated sixth of nine, the weight and ranking are the questions he must answer.

runners_data.name: Ambitious Fellow
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with extensive form at 22-25f on Good ground — shown in midfield on the map due to the congestion of hold-up types in this race, meaning he is unlikely to find his preferred deep position; trainer Fahey is 0/13 past 14 days and his recent string of U/P/F finishes tempers expectation significantly.
runners_data.comment: Ambitious Fellow has been winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up and an unseating among recent outings dampening confidence, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a manageable 27-day break carrying 154 lb.

runners_data.name: Samui
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partnering a Gordon Elliott seven-year-old who has placed multiple times at 14-22f but has a recent slash (01707/) suggesting inconsistency; hood and tongue-tie combination noted, and returning after just 7 days raises a fitness flag even in an Elliott yard, though his sim-going profile shows 2 wins from 15.
runners_data.comment: Samui won four starts back and has run over today's trip, and at 154 lb he arrives fit on a seven-day turnaround — the chief concern is a trainer firing at just 3% in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: The Friday Man
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 384 days off — the most significant flag in this field — partnered by a 7lb claimer for Moses McCabe who has 0/0 entries in the past 14 days; his pace contribution could shape the race but expectations of him threatening must be substantially tempered by the layoff and his declining form figures (0/454-).
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for over a year, The Friday Man faces a stiff ask ranked seventh of nine on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and a couple of fourth places offer some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Gangster Granny
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with four wins from five recent starts on Good ground over 22f, all at the same course type — this is genuinely strong form but her natural running style sits at the back and she has been redistributed to midfield; the congestion of similar types means she may not find the space her style demands, and the style-fit discount applies here.
runners_data.comment: Gangster Granny arrives in good heart with wins last time out and two starts back, but she is ranked bottom of this field on our figures and carries 153 lb, making it hard to fancy her against stronger-rated rivals despite that recent winning thread.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Diamond and The Friday Man are the two confirmed front-runners in this nine-runner field, and with both likely to press for the early lead over 3m on Good to Firm ground at Down Royal, an honest, competitive gallop is the probable outcome rather than a dawdle. Rocky's Diamond, trained by Declan Queally and OR-rated 147, is the higher-class of the two pace-setters and is likely to dominate that duel, while The Friday Man — off 384 days and a 7lb claimer in the plate — is the more vulnerable if the pace heats up at the front. This race holds more prominent and hold-up runners than the map can comfortably place: Ambitious Fellow and Gangster Granny are genuine hold-up types pushed into a midfield slot, and neither is likely to secure their natural deep position with this much traffic ahead of them. The honest gallop set by contested front-runners over a demanding 3m trip strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel smoothly and pick off a tiring leader, giving the tactical edge to horses with a clean jumping style and a proven stamina profile at this sort of pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond and The Friday Man set a genuine gallop that strings the field out and weakens the leaders from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond sets a fair clip but begins to weaken late, allowing prominent stalkers who have raced just off the pace to sweep through and dominate the finish; 3m on Good to Firm ground rewards those who have conserved energy through the first half.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond dictates at a controlled tempo, conserves enough energy, and capitalises on the Good to Firm surface to outstay a weakening field in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A measured pace from the front means less attrition on the leaders, allowing Rocky's Diamond's class advantage over this field to assert itself in the final two flights; the Good to Firm conditions suit a horse who has won on similar going and is fit off a 14-day return.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out sufficiently to leave a gap for a genuine hold-up horse to finish strongly from the rear in the final stages.
scenarios.body: Reverend Hubert or Samui, tracking from rear-midfield, would need the pace collapse to be significant enough to make up ground; note both Ambitious Fellow and Gangster Granny are redistributed from their natural hold-up positions and are less likely to execute this move cleanly in a packed field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Race, Veteran Grinds
scenarios.trigger: If the race deteriorates into a gruelling slog with multiple casualties, leaving a grinder to capitalise on opponents' errors or fatigue over the final mile.
scenarios.body: Thecompanysergeant, a nine-year-old who has won at 20f and placed repeatedly in staying hurdles, is the type to grind through a fractured field if the race falls apart; Reverend Hubert's strong course-form profile on similar ground is also relevant in this unlikely but attritional shape.

watchPoints.text: The Friday Man's fitness after 384 days off is the single biggest race-shaping unknown — if he fades earlier than expected from the front, Rocky's Diamond dictates unopposed and the entire pace dynamic shifts.

Gangster Granny's four recent wins are eye-catching but she is a true hold-up horse in a race where hold-up ground is at a premium — watch whether Kevin Sexton can find daylight or is forced wide from mid-race onwards.

Clay Pigeons has shown all her best form on Soft or Good to Soft; this Good to Firm confirmed surface is her first hard-ground start and Brian Hayes will need to judge whether she travels as fluently as she has on ease.

Loch Cuan and Gangster Granny share very similar course profiles (22f Good, repeat wins) — if both travel prominently, they may end up racing against each other rather than the front-runners, creating a fascinating mid-race battle worth tracking from halfway.

Samui returns just 7 days after his last run — Kennedy's booking suggests Elliott is confident, but monitor how the horse jumps early; if he is flat at the first two flights it may indicate the quick return has left its mark.

races.name: Tayto Group Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jonny Carrol
runners_data.note: Prominent-running five-year-old for McCabe and amateur Herbison(7), solid placing at this 20f-style trip on Good ground but three recent finishes outside the top six and only one place from seven similar-going runs raise doubts about his ceiling in a competitive OR=100 heat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Jonny Carrol does at least arrive on a reasonable turnaround of 21 days and shaped with some promise when third five starts back, though a pulled-up effort four starts back and a run of mid-pack finishes since leave him with plenty to find off 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Journey So Far
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, this Cromwell hold-up type won over 22f on Good but has since drifted back to a ninth, and three Good-going runs from twelve yield only one win — the trend line does not encourage confidence over this stiff 3m trip.
runners_data.comment: Journey So Far advertised his class with a win two starts back and, rated 109, shapes as a serious threat stepping back to a trip he has already encountered; the lengthy absence of 26 days and a burdensome 168 lb ask are the risks to assess.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: Prominent-going seven-year-old for McConnell who handles Good ground extremely well (13 starts, five places), though a run of results showing 8-8-4-5-U recently suggests he finds winning elusive; Torrens takes the ride and straightforward front-end tactics suit the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Charlie's Dilemma has yet to trouble the judge in recent starts, and our rating of 107 makes him one of the most potent threats in this field of 22, with distance experience and a sharp 21-day turnaround working in his favour; the unseating last time and a winless recent run are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with two wins on Good going and a string of placed efforts over comparable trips, making her one of the most solid form-based closers in the field; the question is whether the controlled pace allows her to close from her natural position.
runners_data.comment: Knocknagoran Lady won two starts back and again three starts back, giving her a bright recent profile, but she finished fourth last time out and carries 167 lb here, which is the obvious query against her chance at a rating of 99 versus our figure of 91.

runners_data.name: Midleton Rare
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran aged eight with two wins on Good/Good-to-Firm ground, but a pull of 10 and 9 in recent Good-ground starts is a concern — the amateur Dunseath(7) partnership carries some risk at 36 days since last run.
runners_data.comment: Midleton Rare has run over today's trip and returns after 36 days off carrying 167 lb, but his recent form gives pause — a winner four starts back, he has since pulled up, finished ninth, and was unplaced last time, leaving him needing a significant upturn.

runners_data.name: Astley
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after a long 116-day absence, ran five times without winning on Good or Soft, and the extended layoff combined with a modest track record makes him difficult to trust at face value regardless of position.
runners_data.comment: Astley returns after 116 days off the track carrying a hefty 162 lb, yet our rating of 119 makes him the one to beat among 22 rivals; winless in his last five starts, though a third three starts back hints at ability, and he merits respect on his highest-rated profile.

runners_data.name: Bayonetta
runners_data.note: Consistent placing machine with seven placed efforts from 15 Good-going starts for Quinn; Slevin is a top booking and the horse has run well at this sort of trip before, though the pattern of close-but-no-cigar suggests a similar fate here.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts without a win, Bayonetta has experience over today's trip and returns on a handy 21-day break, but carrying 162 lb looks the sternest test for a mare ranked mid-field here.

runners_data.name: Matter Of Opinion
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with an amateur rider (Byrne, 7lb claim), no wins in recent Good-ground tries, and a history of mid-table finishes — the Harvey yard returns 0/0 over the past 14 days and this looks a difficult opportunity to land.
runners_data.comment: Matter Of Opinion has run over today's trip and returns on a sound 21-day break, yet he remains winless in his last five starts with a best recent finish of fifth, and carrying 160 lb against 21 rivals makes further progress hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Schiehallion
runners_data.note: Aged nine hold-up type whose Good-ground record includes three career pulls and whose recent form shows back-to-back non-completions; McLoughlin's string has had minimal recent runners and confidence in peak fitness is low.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and twice pulled up in his most recent three, Schiehallion faces a stiff ask under 160 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 100 offers a sliver of encouragement for connections.

runners_data.name: Brandt
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up racer by nature who has been mapped to midfield given the depth of closers in this field — Collins's runner has only one win from ten Good-ground tries and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 confirms he is unlikely to race in his optimum role, discounting his chance.
runners_data.comment: Brandt catches the eye on our rating, ranked third in a field of 22 and carrying a figure well clear of his official mark, and he has run over today's trip before; the concern is a winless recent spell and a return from 80 days off.

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: Prominent-going mare for McConnell with one win and six places from 15 Good-ground starts — an excellent fit for the race shape — and Halford(7) takes the ride; placed at 22f and 24f recently, she shapes as a natural on-pace participant who can benefit from the controlled fractions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but that second two starts back and a third four starts back hint at ability, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the burden of 158 lb looks the chief obstacle to reversing her slide.

runners_data.name: Grace Faraday
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground at 24f previously, but returns after 98 days off and was unsighted at her most recent start; her natural hold-up style means she has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map — the fitness query after the layoff is the primary concern, independent of the positional redistribution.
runners_data.comment: Grace Faraday won in her last five starts but unseated last time out, and that jumping blunder — combined with 98 days off the track — makes fitness a query; she has run over today's trip and a mark of 90 gives her a chance if shaken up.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Kennedy is a top-tier booking for Elliott who returned 1/30 over 14 days, and Sneddy Eddie is a recent winner on Good going — but his natural closer's instinct has been displaced by the field's depth of hold-up types, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 signals he is unlikely to race from his preferred rear position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 158 lb, Sneddy Eddie is hard to fancy at face value, though he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and a 19-day turnaround suggests he returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Curling, running off just 13 days with strong Good-surface form (2W, 5P from 15 similar-going runs); dictating on a flat, sound 3m course unchallenged sets up a genuine wire-to-wire opportunity, and Kenneally(5) needs to simply stay out of trouble and maintain rhythm.
runners_data.comment: Fire Coral has pulled up in recent starts and finished eighth last time out, making her hard to fancy ranked 16 of 22 on our figures, though she has experience over today's trip and going, and a win five starts back offers slim residual encouragement.

runners_data.name: Technology
runners_data.note: McConnell's nine-year-old hold-up type forced into a midfield map position, returning from 49 days off with recent form showing a fall and a non-completion — the STYLE_FIT of 0.91 signals further compromise and the record on Good ground (0 wins from 13) does not inspire.
runners_data.comment: Technology has been winless in his last five starts, though a second five starts back shows he can get involved, and he has run over today's trip before; the fall two starts back clouds his profile, and 49 days off the track adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Moonshine Girl
runners_data.note: Regular placer at 22-24f on Good ground with three such efforts from 15 runs, trained by Gilligan and ridden by Gilligan(5) — a family combination; her true hold-up nature is squeezed by the field's density, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 reflects racing out of role.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 19th of 22 on our figures, Moonshine Girl is hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and a return to action after just 18 days; the 148 lb burden does her no favours either.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Five-year-old winner on Good ground over 20f, carrying a blinkered headgear flag and mapping as a redistributed hold-up type; Rothwell has placed three runners from 12 in the past fortnight, suggesting modest current yard form, though this youngster with one win has upside if given a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Clever Court's recent form makes him hard to fancy, with two pulled-up efforts in his last five starts and finishes of seventh and ninth since his win three starts back; the return after 21 days and distance experience offer little consolation.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: Returning after just six days between runs, this eight-year-old hold-up type wears a hood and has one win from 15 Good-going tries; the tight turnaround and moderate strike-rate make him hard to support, and racing further forward than natural (STYLE_FIT 0.92) adds another layer of difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 20 of 22 on our figures, Whatyouwant faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and the six-day turnaround suggests she is at least fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Gypsy Poet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with zero wins or places from six Good-going starts and no headgear advantage — the Doyle yard has had minimal recent runners and there is nothing in the form or profile to suggest a step forward here, compounded by a midfield map that does not reflect her natural rear position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 21 of 22 on our figures, Gypsy Poet makes a difficult case; he has run over today's trip before and returns after 49 days off, but his recent string of unplaced efforts offers little encouragement at 143 lb.

runners_data.name: Sekifi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a finish-fading flag and a non-completion on his latest start, returning from 47 days off; the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 reflects the mismatch between his natural rear running and where he will be forced to sit — the form and fitness picture are both uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out and winless in his last five starts, Sekifi is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked 18 of 22, though he has run over today's trip before and the 47-day break may have him freshened up.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: No jockey listed publicly, returns after 35 days with a recent non-completion record and runs without notable headgear — a true hold-up runner repositioned to midfield by the field's density; career stats show 0 wins from multiple Good-going attempts and this shapes as an each-way longshot at best.
runners_data.comment: My Policy has pulled up in three of her last five starts, including her two most recent outings, and is yet to win in that spell, which makes confidence hard to muster; a second three starts back offers some encouragement, but 153 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Experienced ten-year-old with two wins and three places from 15 Good-going starts over long trips — the form profile is genuinely competitive, but his natural hold-up style has been pushed forward by the field's composition (STYLE_FIT 0.93), and the Kelly yard has been quiet at 1/11 over 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Fire Coral is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field and, facing no genuine pace pressure from another leader, will control tempo from the front on Good to Firm ground over 3m at Down Royal. With Jonny Carrol and Charlie's Dilemma likely to push forward from the prominent group, Fire Coral will still dictate the fractions and set what figures to be a measured, galloping pace suited to a true staying test rather than an explosive finish. The overwhelming majority of this field are hold-up or midfield types who will need the pace to collapse in the final circuit to close, yet the steady controlled gallop Fire Coral creates is unlikely to produce that late implosion. Note that the field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Brandt, Sneddy Eddie, Grace Faraday, Moonshine Girl, Clever Court and several others are genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would naturally prefer, compromising their finishing kicks. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can track Fire Coral through the race and stay on strongly, or disciplined midfield travellers who carry an outstanding fitness and staying profile, will benefit most — positional races from mid-to-front are favoured, and late-closing patterns from far back are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fire Coral Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Fire Coral goes unchallenged at the head of affairs and the holding Good to Firm surface rewards bold front-running over 3m.
scenarios.body: Fire Coral dictates a sustainable gallop, jumps fluently, and the chasing pack simply cannot reel in a horse who has controlled all the fractions; on a flat, sound surface the Curling-trained seven-year-old has both the fitness marker of a recent run 13 days ago and strong sim-going form to draw on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is honest enough to anchor the front-runners but not so fierce that it burns them off, allowing a handy prominent tracker to pounce between the last two flights.
scenarios.body: Charlie's Dilemma and Jonny Carrol, both suited to a strongly-run 3m on Good ground and both possessing strong Good-to-Good form, stalk Fire Coral before hitting the front running to the final hurdle; this shape negates the back-of-the-field pack whose closers cannot produce a devastating late burst over this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough from the front to set up a true staying finish that allows a well-ridden closer to thread through tired rivals in the straight.
scenarios.body: Knocknagoran Lady — a two-time winner at comparable distances on Good ground — or Bayonetta, who has accumulated seven places on similar going, could be produced late if rivals have over-committed jumping the final two; this scenario is structurally discounted because many apparent closers have been displaced forward in the field and will lack the fuel to close from genuinely far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If attrition strikes the field late and several front-end horses tie up, allowing a resolute mid-pack stayer to pick off tired rivals close home.
scenarios.body: Sneddy Eddie, a recent winner on Good ground with Kennedy aboard and Elliott's in-form operation, or Le Grand Vert, a proven 3m performer with course-relevant placing form, could benefit if the field strings out and tired jumping creates gaps late on; both are flagged as redistributed true hold-up types forced to race nearer the pace than ideal, which tempers this scenario's likelihood despite their individual form claims.

watchPoints.text: Fire Coral must be monitored at every hurdle — if the sole front-runner jumps sloppily or is pushed wide at any point, the controlled gallop evaporates and the entire pace dynamic shifts fundamentally.

Jonny Carrol and Charlie's Dilemma are the most likely horses to press forward and sit on Fire Coral's quarters; if either tests the pace aggressively in the early stages, the race tempo could rise sharply and dramatically shorten Fire Coral's chance.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Sneddy Eddie, Brandt, Grace Faraday, Moonshine Girl and Clever Court — will all be forced to race nearer the pace than ideal; watch for crowding and traffic incidents on the first circuit in a 22-runner field on Good to Firm ground.

runners_data.name: Clovelly Charm
runners_data.comment: Clovelly Charm won last time out and, with just two starts to her name, remains unexposed and open to plenty of improvement; the 47-day absence is the main query under a big 165 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Missouri Snow
runners_data.comment: Missouri Snow arrives in red-hot form, winning her last two starts in succession, and 22 days between runs suggests she comes here fresh and ready; the chief concern is whether 165 lb at the top of the weights will blunt her momentum.

runners_data.name: Hilly Filly
runners_data.comment: Hilly Filly won on her sole recent start and remains unexposed, but 49 days off the track and a trainer without a winner in the last 14 days are factors to weigh against her at 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Bredas Pearl
runners_data.comment: Bredas Pearl arrives here in fine fettle after consecutive placed efforts, third two starts back and second last time out, and has run over today's trip before. Winless in her last three, she nonetheless profiles as the one to beat on her rating heading a field of 12.

runners_data.name: Bresil Belle
runners_data.comment: Bresil Belle makes her debut carrying 158 lb, completely unexposed and with everything still to prove — a mare to watch closely as she finds her feet in the race environment.

runners_data.name: Cave Daisy
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Cave Daisy steps into the unknown carrying 158 lb, but her unraced profile leaves plenty to work with and she could be anything as connections find out what they have.

runners_data.name: Maxdale Prinxess
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Maxdale Prinxess carries 158 lb into the unknown but remains open to any amount of improvement as connections find out what she is capable of at this first opportunity.

runners_data.name: Poet's Creek
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to any amount of improvement on debut, Poet's Creek is yet to score under rules and arrives carrying 158 lb, leaving the imagination free to fill in the gaps.

runners_data.name: Anna Quaintance
runners_data.comment: Anna Quaintance has run over today's trip and, rated 74 among these rivals, she represents a live threat back over a proven distance — the concern is that her fifth last time out leaves her yet to score in recent starts and she will need to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Hutton Star
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Hutton Star steps onto the track carrying 155 lb with everything still to prove but with all questions still to be answered by the racecourse.

runners_data.name: Junction Road
runners_data.comment: Unraced and open to plenty of improvement, Junction Road steps into the unknown on debut carrying 155 lb, with her unexposed profile leaving plenty to work with as connections find out what she is capable of.

runners_data.name: Molly Des Bruyeres
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Molly Des Bruyeres is yet to score under rules and arrives as an unknown quantity, but carrying 155 lb is the key physical challenge she faces first time out.
